title: Priyanka Chopra Is Worth ₹2,507 Crore. She's the Only Woman on Fortune India's Cover.
excerpt: The inaugural Fortune India–Interbrand ranking puts a Bvlgari ambassador and Rajamouli star alongside Virat Kohli and Shah Rukh Khan. In a list of 25 most valuable celebrities, she stands conspicuously alone.
body:
When Fortune India released its inaugural Most Valuable Celebrities ranking this week — a collaboration with global brand consultancy Interbrand — nobody was shocked to see **Virat Kohli** at the top. The man's brand value sits at ₹3,542 crore, and at this point, questioning his dominance feels like arguing with weather.

What was worth noticing, though, was the company he keeps.

**Shah Rukh Khan** claimed the second spot at ₹3,017 crore, which sounds about right for a man who can sell cars, streaming subscriptions, and an entire national mood with a single raised eyebrow. But it's the third name that tells the real story: **Priyanka Chopra Jonas**, valued at ₹2,507 crore, the only woman to receive a standalone cover in Fortune India's June 2026 issue — and the highest-ranked female celebrity on the entire list.

Three covers. Three faces. Two are men who've dominated Indian culture for decades. The third is a woman who decided India wasn't big enough and went global.

## The Numbers Don't Lie

The Fortune India–Interbrand methodology goes deeper than endorsement cheques and Instagram followers. It measures distinctiveness, engagement, trust, affinity, coherence, and responsibility — essentially, how much of a living, breathing brand you are. By that measure, Priyanka isn't just popular. She's a portfolio.

Consider: her partnerships with **Bvlgari** and **Bentley** aren't the kind of deals you land by being famous. They're the kind you land by being trusted across continents, the kind where your face represents a century-old luxury house and nobody blinks. She's one of the few Indian celebrities whose name carries the same weight in a boardroom in Milan as it does at a press junket in Mumbai.

> "Her work as a producer, entrepreneur, investor and philanthropist has enabled her to build a brand that transcends industries and geographies." — Fortune India–Interbrand report

The rest of the top 10 reads like a hall of fame carved into marble: **MS Dhoni** at 4th (because retirement means nothing when you're Dhoni), **Ranveer Singh** at 5th riding the ₹3,000 crore Dhurandhar wave, **Akshay Kumar** at 6th, **Amitabh Bachchan** at 7th proving that legends don't depreciate, **Sachin Tendulkar** at 8th, **Alia Bhatt** at 9th, and **Allu Arjun** rounding out the top 10 — proof that Telugu cinema's commercial explosion has a name and a face.

Scroll further and you find **Deepika Padukone** at 11th, **Rashmika Mandanna** at 17th, and names like **Diljit Dosanjh**, **Arijit Singh**, **Karan Johar**, **Vicky Kaushal**, women's cricket star **Smriti Mandhana**, and **Nayanthara** also making the 25.

But let's not sugarcoat it: out of India's 25 most valuable celebrities, only a handful are women. Priyanka at 3 isn't just a personal triumph. It's a commentary on how much space women actually occupy in the brand ecosystem, even in 2026.

## The Varanasi Factor

What makes Priyanka's placement especially interesting right now is timing. She's deep into filming **S.S. Rajamouli's Varanasi** — a time-travel action epic co-starring **Mahesh Babu** and **Prithviraj Sukumaran** — with six months of shooting still remaining in Hyderabad. This isn't a cameo or a "global star does a song" arrangement. This is a full-blown Rajamouli lead, the kind of role that has historically turned actors into institutions. Baahubali made Prabhas a global name. RRR put Jr NTR and Ram Charan in rooms with Steven Spielberg. Varanasi could do something similar for Priyanka — except she's already been in those rooms.

She shared a glimpse of her downtime recently from the Hyderabad set: poolside in black swimwear, a face mask, a bowl of jamun, and the IPL final on a big screen with an RCB sticker slapped on. Even her breaks look like a brand campaign.

## What This Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs watching from New York, London, or Toronto, this ranking confirms what they've sensed for years: Indian celebrity culture has become genuinely global infrastructure. Kohli sells sportswear on five continents. SRK's face launches hotel chains. And Priyanka sits on boards you've actually heard of, produces content for streaming platforms you actually use, and shows up in franchise films your non-Indian friends also watch.

The Fortune India list isn't a vanity project. It's a measure of who India exports as cultural capital — and in 2026, that export list runs on cricket, cinema, and one woman who figured out you don't have to choose a hemisphere.

Miss World, 2000. Bollywood queen, 2008. Quantico, 2015. Hollywood lead, 2020. Fortune India cover star, 2026. Twenty-six years and the arc still bends upward. The only question left is what the next line on the résumé looks like — and if Rajamouli has anything to say about it, it's going to be very, very big.
